chunks: And it was also narrated - from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan, from Salih ibn Abi al-Aswad, from Abi al-Jarud, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
"There is no specific amount fixed upon al-Safa."

key_terms.الصَّفَا: Al-Safa, one of the two hills between which pilgrims walk during Sa'i.
key_terms.مُوَقَّتٌ: Fixed, determined, or specified (in terms of quantity or time).

ai.seo_question: What is the fixed number of circuits required for Sa'i between Safa and Marwah?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that while the Sa'i between Safa and Marwah is a prescribed ritual, there is no fixed, mandatory number of circuits (such as the seven commonly practiced) strictly required by the text itself, allowing for flexibility. This ruling highlights the distinction between the essential pillar (rukn) of the ritual and the customary practice (sunnah) that later became standard, reflecting the Shia scholarly view on the permissibility of varying the number of rounds as long as the act is performed. It underscores the principle that not all ritual details are rigidly quantified in the primary sources, leaving room for juristic interpretation regarding the completeness of the Hajj or Umrah rites.
